newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reunert half yr shr falls 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Reunert half yr shr falls 15 pct.

text.p: South African technology group Reunert Ltd said on Wednesday half year earnings per share after abnormal items were down 15 percent to 39.4 cents.
Before the abnormal items, earnings were unchanged at last year's 46.3 cents a share.
An unchanged interim dividend of 11 cents was declared.
Reunert said in a statement that abnormal items of 13.8 million rand was mainly related to the cost of restructuring its Consolidated Lamp Manufacturers unit.
Directors repeated chairman Clive Parker's prediction earlier this year that second half earnings would improve but not sufficiently to compensate for the first half decline.
Directors said the telecommunications companies had strong order books which would see them through until year end.
The pace of growth in electrical engineering, defence and allied, and consumer and commercial divisions was not expected to change markedly during the next few months.

"The group anticipates the six months to September will yield better results but the improvement is unlikely to be strong enough to compensate for the profit reduction during the first half of the financial year," Reunert said.

In the six months under review turnover was up seven percent to 2.4 billion rand but difficult market conditions kept operating margins in check leaving operating profit before abnormal items nine percent lower at 128.4 million rand.
Interest costs rose 19 percent to 14.3 million rand and the tax rate grew to 41 percent mainly because of the structure at the lamp business.

Boet Pretorius, Reunert's new chief executive said the restructuring of the telecommunications division was bearing fruit, with improvements in demand from parastatal telecommunications unit, Telkom, translating into substantial order flows.
He said Reunert looked forward to developing good relations with SBC Communications Inc, Telkom's new equity partner, although SBC had yet to "show its hand" in regard to suppliers.
Last month South Africa's government signed a deal with a consortium comprising SBC and Telekom Malaysia Bhd to sell a 30-percent stake in the concern for $1.26 billion.
